structured_output.message:
1. Identity fields: the composite of (a) source concept identity + its registered version — `consumer-b@v1`, pinned at registration time and not re-derived on later target-supersede events — and (b) the typed locator, i.e. both locator type and locator target (`@concept:shared-target`). Locator type+target alone is not identity: two owners can legitimately hold the same locator, so matching on locator alone would conflate distinct instances.

2. A local removal must retire exactly the single (source, locator) tuple belonging to the remover, and nothing else. It must not: (a) deactivate, alter, or otherwise affect any other owner's instance sharing that locator — specifically, B's instance must remain active when another owner removes its own; (b) be treated as concept-retire migration evidence for any owner other than the one performing the removal; (c) suppress or reroute the target-supersede response owed to instances that remain active — B, still active, must receive its correct target-supersede response independent of another owner's removal.

3. Source-less historical events must remain foldable and must replay to the same lifecycle state they produced before the source field existed — this is a positive backward-compatibility guarantee, not merely non-deletion. Absence of source must not be treated as "match any owner": a wildcard legacy row must not be clobbered by any single owner's scoped removal. Absence of source should resolve to a distinct, deterministic legacy identity, separate from any owner's namespaced (source, locator) instance.

4. Any downstream fold or auxiliary event that currently keys on locator alone must instead carry/key on the full (source, locator) composite. This applies at minimum to: the target-supersede response/notification (must be delivered per-instance so B's still-active instance gets its own, uncontaminated by other owners' removals); update/supersede auxiliary events (must carry enough identity — source + locator — to affect only B); the concept-retire migration-evidence fold (must not accept another owner's removal as evidence for B's retirement); and any active-instance projection, dedup, or aggregation currently keyed on locator alone.

I refuse any contract resting on locator-only matching or that silently drops legacy (source-less) compatibility, per B's stated veto.

refuse any contract that silently drops source-less legacy event compatibility
source-less historical events must resolve to a distinct deterministic legacy identity, not a wildcard match

Whether other owners' existing legacy rows carry a source field or are source-less
